# split_v3 gate values — what the rebuild is read against

**Generated by `scripts/analysis/split_v3_gate_reference.py`.** Regenerate it;
do not edit. Every number is read out of the split_v3 run that produced it.

These are **what split_v3 achieved**, not thresholds anyone set. A split_v4 run
that misses one is not necessarily wrong — the labels changed, and the point of
the rebuild is that the porosity should be better. The table exists so a
difference is SEEN and explained rather than missed.

## ldm06 — the LDM


### run-0001, base, step 130000 — 5 check(s), last at step 130000

| gate | ema_ddim50 | raw_ddim50 | reading |
|---|---|---|---|
| porosity MAE | 0.001119 | 0.001083 | delivered against requested |
| delivered phi mean | 0.01226 | 0.01235 | over all buckets |
| std ratio (mu-normalised) | 1.8006 | 1.7994 | scored against the SAMPLED reference 1.863, not 1.0 |
| x0 clamp saturation | 1.09e-07 | 1.06e-07 | off-manifold diagnostic |
| air mean | 0.05480 | 0.05479 | exterior air the request asked for |
| degenerate cells | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0 is the only acceptable value |

**Kill switch** — asked 0.005 and 0.05: ema delivered 0.00487 and 0.04912, separation 0.04425, direction_ok True. A model that cannot separate two requested porosities is not conditioning at all.

**Inset-surface gates**: `outside_air_gt_0.95` True, `inside_air_lt_0.02` True, `surface_error_lt_4vox` True, `all_pass` True

**Conditioning alive** (MAD as % of the noise MAD 1.992): porosity 2.97 %, orientation 2.14 %, neighbours 8.74 %. A conditioning input whose ablation moves nothing is not being used.

Added in split_v4: JI_11 (train)


## How the v4 chain uses these

`scripts/chain_v8_split_v4.sh` runs the same checks as stages and writes a
PASS/FAIL line per gate into `runs/campaigns/chain.log`, against this file.
A FAIL does not stop the chain — the labels changed and a moved number may be
the improvement the rebuild is for — except for `degen`, the kill switch's
`direction_ok`, and a non-finite loss, which mean the run is not working.
